simple.meaning: צוֹפַר (Tsôwphar) is a Hebrew word meaning “Tsophar , a friend of Job.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: צוֹפַר (H6691) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 2:11, with occurrences in Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צוֹפַר (H6691) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in צוֹפַר (H6691) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: צוֹפַר (Tsôwphar) / H6691 is traced through Job 2:11, Job 11:1, Job 20:1, Job 42:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
